_about: Config for .github/scripts/{build,check,smoke}_release_tree.py (#2705, ported from claude-remember#851). The `release` branch is what the Anthropic plugin directory fetches; master keeps everything. See docs/releasing.md.
_deny_why: Deny-list, not allow-list: a path forgotten here ships and is caught loudly by the size/count check; a path forgotten in an allow-list would vanish from users' installs silently. Entry ending in '/' = directory prefix, otherwise an exact path.
_kept_why: _shipped_reference.py is NOT denied: it is the fallback _shipped_config() reads when .supertool.json is absent beside _supertool.py (the pip-install route, #1783) -- and this release tree denies .supertool.json, so the fallback is load-bearing here. .mcp.json ships because it registers the claude-channel notifier the plugin manifest declares.
_keep_why: Exact-path carve-out that wins over a denied prefix (#2729). hooks/shipped_rules.py reads these two files at runtime from $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT for the one shipped jit-context guard rule (supertool-no-cut.md); .claude/ denies the whole directory they live in, so a release install shipped the rule disabled with nothing saying so. shipped_rules.py's own docstring: the rule files are not copied, the same bytes the jit hooks read in this checkout are what a plugin install reads too -- so the fix is to let exactly these two through rather than relocate the source and keep a second copy in sync by hand. Nothing else under .claude/ ships; is_kept() is exact-path only, no prefix.
_budget_why: max_file_bytes and max_files are the directory's own rules (pre-submission checklist, 'Files in the plugin folder'); images and fonts are exempt from the per-file limit. max_total_bytes is this repository's own ceiling: comment/docstring stripping (#2731) took the built tree from 6,887,694 to 3,495,927 bytes (measured on HEAD, 2026-10-03); 4 MiB leaves about 600 KiB of headroom over that for growth before the next release.
_exceptions_why: A declared exception lets check_release_tree.py report a REVIEW line instead of a FAIL for a named, issue-referenced path over max_file_bytes. Any other oversize file still fails -- this is not a second deny-list.
_ladder_inline_why: #2732: COMMAND_SCRIPT_NOT_FOLLOWED -- the directory's own scanner stops at a shipped script it cannot follow, and `source`/`.` of a sibling file is a confirmed cause (claude-jit-context's docs/directory-validator.md). hooks/python-ladder.sh is sourced by both consumers below in the committed tree (readability, one definition); build_release_tree.py inlines its body into each consumer and drops the file from what ships, so nothing in the release tree sources anything.
_release_readme_why: #2732: MCP_FORWARDS_CREDENTIAL_ENV's text-only half -- the full README's security section and command examples read as credential-handling/attack text to the directory's scanner. README.release.md is a short, variable-free, URL-free (one real link excepted) description swapped in for README.md at build time; the full README never ships to the directory at all.
_notifiers_deny_why: #2732, from a second validator pass on the full tree. notifiers/claude-channel/README.md and install.sh are human-facing setup docs for a human running them by hand -- the MCP server itself is registered and started by .mcp.json's own command, never by install.sh, and neither file is read at runtime. notifiers/cursor-witness/ is a VS Code extension this repository's own .supertool.json wires in as a dev-only notifier for working on supertool itself; .supertool.json is already denied above and _shipped_reference.py (the fallback a plugin install actually reads) never wires cursor-witness in, so a plugin install never activates it -- the whole directory, icon.png included, ships to no purpose.
